outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo said Saturday, Nov 14, hourly rolling blackouts of 1.5 to 3 queues will again be in effect around the clock in some regions, with industrial capacity limits also in place, after the same format was used throughout Friday, Nov 13. Ukrenergo and Ukraine's Energy Ministry said Friday that Russian attacks left consumers without power in 12 regions: Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, Zhytomyr, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Rivne, Sumy, Kharkiv, Khmelnytsky, and Chernihiv. Chernihivoblenergo said a Russian attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts; crews would start repairs when the security situation allows. Regional operators also reported emergency cuts Friday in parts of the Kyiv region (Bucha, Fastiv, Bila Tserkva, and Obukhiv districts) and in the Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Chernihiv, and Cherkasy regions. UA.NEWS, citing earlier figures, said nearly 700,000 households remained without power as of Nov 12.

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit (multiple thermal units offline or in maintenance), plus a Friday transmission-line trip that briefly isolated Granma
outages.affected: 1,930 MW forecast to be affected at peak on Nov 13 (1,900 MW deficit), according to UNE's morning bulletin. At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time, 900 MW was available, demand was 2,142 MW, and 1,245 MW was already affected; UNE estimated 1,600 MW affected at midday. Thursday's maximum affectation was 1,920 MW at 7:00 p.m. The morning forecast listed several thermal units offline or in maintenance, including Guiteras, Felton, Santa Cruz, Renté, and Nuevitas. CubaNet, citing a later UNE note, said unit 2 of the Ernesto Guevara plant in Santa Cruz went offline at 8:55 a.m. Cuba time due to an oil leak in a turbine bearing, leaving all three units at that plant out of service; that failure was not included in the morning peak forecast. On Friday, a fault on the 110 kV line to Santiago de Cuba fully disconnected Granma province from the national grid; the Electric Company of Granma said the province was reconnected at 1:27 p.m. Cuba time and had 20 MW in service at 1:50 p.m., with restoration continuing gradually. Las Tunas was isolated at midday by the National Load Dispatch and resynchronized at 1:24 p.m. with 15 MW, according to the provincial utility as reported by El Alambique and CiberCuba. No later official UNE figure for the actual evening peak was found as of Friday evening CT.
outages.updated: Nov 13, 2026, 6:03 p.m. (El Alambique timestamp; UNE morning bulletin and Friday afternoon provincial utility notices)

outages.cause: Widespread, ongoing grid failures after years of underinvestment, worsened by June earthquakes
outages.affected: No official customer count. Bloomberg Línea reported Nov 13 that outages are worsening nationwide, with Mérida, Táchira, and Trujillo among the hardest hit; Caracas is largely spared the worst cuts. A late-September Meganálisis survey cited in that report found 87% of respondents lost power at least four days a week, and nearly four in five said cuts usually lasted more than three hours. Interim President Delcy Rodríguez said the June earthquakes took about 800 MW of generation offline, of which 600 MW had been restored.
outages.updated: Nov 13, 2026, 12:04 a.m.; rechecked Friday evening CT, no later official customer count found

outages.cause: National generation shortfall during evening peak; Tarbela hydropower about 800 MW below normal after reduced water releases following the fifth-extension incident, plus seasonal hydrology and LNG limits
outages.affected: About 1,500 MW national shortfall during evening peak on Nov 11 (peak demand about 16,000 MW vs. about 14,500 MW available), according to ISMO figures cited Nov 12. ISMO said the Nov 10 shortfall, which reached about 2,530 MW, had eased and that generation was back to the routine plan as of Nov 11, but the 1,500 MW evening-peak gap (5 p.m. to 11 p.m.) remained. Discos were following existing 1.5 to 2 hour load-management schedules; The Nation reported some areas still facing up to five hours of additional load-shedding. No later official ISMO update was found as of Friday evening CT.
outages.updated: Nov 12, 2026; no later official ISMO update found as of Friday evening CT

outages.place: Mayfair, Crosby, Homestead Park, Mayfair West, and nearby suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after overnight restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. The cause of the Mayfair fire is being investigated
outages.affected: No official customer count. City Power said power restored overnight to essential services and some residential and industrial customers was lost again when Hursthill tripped early Friday. The outage again affected the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, Sentech, residents in Crosby, Homestead Park, Mayfair, and Mayfair West, and about 50% of customers in Crown's industrial area. No later Friday evening official update was found after City Power's midday statement.
outages.etr: City Power said Friday it would gradually restore supply during the day and into the weekend, depending on network stability
outages.updated: Nov 13, 2026, 12:02 p.m. SAST (4:02 a.m. CT); rechecked Friday evening CT, no later official update found

outages.cause: A transmission line trip triggered an under-frequency load shedding event, according to Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro
outages.affected: About 50,000 Newfoundland Power customers were without electricity at the peak. CBC reported that power was restored shortly before 5 p.m. NT. VOCM said the outage earlier Friday afternoon affected pockets of customers on the Avalon Peninsula, the Burin Peninsula, in central Newfoundland, and on the west coast.
outages.etr: Restored shortly before 5 p.m. NT (2:30 p.m. CT)
outages.updated: Nov 13, 2026, shortly before 5 p.m. NT (2:30 p.m. CT)
